nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of NiMoO4 cuboids
nodes.procedure: The commercial nickel foam was successively washed with ethanol, a 1 M HCl aqueous solution and deionized water. One piece of nickel foam (1 × 3 cm²) was immersed into 15 ml of H2O containing Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.04 M) and (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O (0.01 M) in a Teflon autoclave. The autoclave was heated at 150 °C for 6 h in a drying oven. After washing with deionized water, the NiMoO4 cuboids were achieved on the nickel foam.

nodes.source_text: To synthesize the MoNi4 electrocatalyst, NiMoO4 cuboids were first constructed on nickel foam through a hydrothermal reaction... After washing with deionized water, the NiMoO4 cuboids were achieved on the nickel foam.

nodes.name: Calcination to form MoNi4/MoO2
nodes.procedure: The as-constructed NiMoO4 cuboids were heated at 500 °C for 2 h in a H2/Ar (4:96) atmosphere, and then, the MoNi4 electrocatalyst anchored on the MoO2 cuboids was obtained. The loading weight of the formed MoNi4 nanoparticles and MoO2 cuboids on the nickel foam was ~43.4 mg cm^-2.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of precursor on Ni foam indexed to NiMoO4 (Supplementary Fig. 6).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction characterization reveals that the crystalline structure of the as-obtained precursor on the Ni foam can be indexed to NiMoO4 (Supplementary Fig. 6).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows dense NiMoO4 cuboids with sizes 0.5-1.0 μm and lengths of tens of microns vertically aligned on nickel foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of NiMoO4 was scrutinized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). As shown in Supplementary Figs 7 and 8, dense NiMoO4 cuboids with sizes in the range of 0.5-1.0 μm and lengths of tens of microns are vertically aligned on the nickel foam.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms NiMoO4 cuboids consist of Ni, Mo, O with Ni:Mo molar ratio ~1:1.01.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping, energy dispersive spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirm that the NiMoO4 cuboids consist of Ni, Mo and O elements, and the molar ratio of Ni to Mo is ~1:1.01.

The peaks located at 26.3°, 37.0°, 41.5°, 49.5°, 53.7°, 60.5° and 66.9° are indexed to metallic MoO2 (JCPDS, No. 32-0671). The appearance of peaks at 31.0° and 43.5° are assigned to the (200) and (121) facets of MoNi4 (JCPDS, No. 65-5480).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals numerous nanoparticles 20-100 nm uniformly anchored on cuboids vertically aligned on nickel foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2a–c, numerous nanoparticles with sizes in the range of 20-100 nm are uniformly anchored on the cuboids, which are vertically aligned on the nickel foam.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes of 0.35 nm for MoO2 (110) facet and 0.28 nm for MoNi4 (200) facet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Clearly, the HRTEM images of the samples show lattice fringes with lattice distances of 0.35 and 0.28 nm, which correspond to the (110) facet of MoO2 and the (200) facet of MoNi4, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX confirms products composed of Mo, Ni, O with Mo:Ni molar ratio ~1:1.3; STEM-EDX shows surface nanoparticles Mo:Ni atomic ratio 1:3.84.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) analysis further confirms that the products are composed of Mo, Ni and O, and the molar ratio of Mo to Ni is ~1:1.3 ... scanning TEM–EDX characterizations indicate that the surface nanoparticles are constituted by only Mo and Ni with an atomic ratio of 1:3.84.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Mo, Ni, O with Mo:Ni molar ratio ~1:1.1; shows metallic Mo0 at 229.3 eV and Ni0 at 852.5 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS spectrum confirms the presence of Mo, Ni and O, and the molar ratio of Mo to Ni is ~1:1.1 ... XPS peaks of metallic Mo0 and Ni0 are observed at 229.3 and 852.5 eV, respectively.
